task: Prepare me for a meeting with Monday.com (monday.com)

key.question: What did monday.com report for Q3 2026 (Nov 9, 2026), and what is the Q4 and full-year guidance? Was growth accelerating or slowing?
key.answer: Q3 revenue was $377.5M, up 19% YoY, and beat the $368–370M guide. Non-GAAP operating margin was a record 24% (non-GAAP operating income $89.4M); GAAP operating income was $31.2M. Q4 guide is $380–382M, only about 14% YoY, so growth is decelerating sharply. FY26 guide is $1,473–1,475M (about 20%), non-GAAP operating margin about 18%, and adjusted FCF $282–288M. Net dollar retention is 108%. Paid customers with more than 10 users number 65,965, up only 5%. Customers above $100K ARR number 2,127, up 33%. RPO is $946M, up 27%. Co-CEOs warned of 'near-term operational headwinds' from the AI-first shift.

key.question: What restructuring or layoffs has monday.com announced in 2026, and what are the cost and organizational effects?
key.answer: In July 2026 monday.com announced a '2026 Restructuring Plan' cutting about 20% of staff (reported as roughly 600–620 jobs; press counts vary). It expected about $45–55M in restructuring charges and raised its FY26 margin target. Restructuring charges were $9.96M in Q3 and $31.4M year to date. Co-founder Eran Zinman called it the hardest decision since the company's founding. Coverage says the AI reorganization is also pushing out managers. The company's own risk language says the plan may not deliver the expected benefits. Verify exact headcount against the company's 6-K.

key.question: What is the strategic priority now, and how far along is the AI product push?
key.answer: monday.com describes itself as 'the AI workspace that turns strategy into execution, at scale' and says it is becoming 'AI-first'. AI products (AI credits, agents, vibe) reached $36M AI ARR in Q3 2026. The company is also investing in enterprise go-to-market, with 123 customers above $500K ARR, up 58%. It announced the One AI acquisition in April 2026 alongside Q1 results. Its other lines include monday CRM, service and dev.

key.question: What competitive, market and stock-price pressures is monday.com visibly facing?
key.answer: On Feb 9, 2026 the stock fell about 22% after Q4 2025 results and guidance. Capital One downgraded it to Equal-weight after the Q2 report because Q3 guidance was cautious. The stock is down sharply in 2026, with sources citing roughly 37–50% or more year to date. This fits the broader SaaS worry that AI will erode seat-based software. Its risk factors cite competition, heavy dependence on work management revenue, and reliance on search and AI-generated traffic. Q4 guidance of about 14% growth deepens the slowdown concern. Exact YTD declines come from aggregators and should be checked.

key.question: Who leads the company and was there any leadership change?
key.answer: Co-founders Roy Mann and Eran Zinman are co-CEOs, and Eliran Glazer is CFO; all three are quoted in the Nov 9, 2026 release. I found no CEO change in my search. The risk factors flag dependence on the founders and a founder share with veto rights. For the meeting, ask the seller to confirm the owners of the relevant area (for example the CRO or CPO) on the IR and leadership pages.

key.question: What are the legal entity, listing and filing status, and is there any distress, going-concern or regulatory issue?
key.answer: The entity is monday.com Ltd., an Israeli company listed on NASDAQ as MNDY. It is a foreign private issuer that files 6-Ks and a 20-F; the FY2025 20-F was filed Mar 13, 2026. The SEC CIK is 1845338. The company is profitable on both a non-GAAP and GAAP basis and generates positive FCF, and I found no going-concern warning or debt distress. The company has a repurchase program. Israel-region conflict is a listed risk factor. I did not run sanctions or enforcement screens, so run those separately if compliance needs them.

key.question: What are the best discovery angles for a seller given the evidence?
key.answer: (1) Ask how the 20% headcount cut and AI-first reorganization are changing buying authority, vendor consolidation and priorities, since the company is cost-disciplined with record margins. (2) Ask how it plans to reaccelerate growth from about 14% in Q4 and lift low net retention of 108%, through enterprise go-to-market and moving up-market. (3) Ask how it is scaling AI agents and credits beyond the current $36M AI ARR, and what it needs on cost, data or integration. Fit is strongest for products that save cost, support enterprise go-to-market or speed up AI delivery.
